Provenance.paintoverNote: c7 (seed+7, round-2 escalation) -- a receding stone tunnel corridor with warm ember light at its far end, closely mirroring mine-backdrop's own tunnel-recession composition. Round 1 (c0-c3) universally drew single close-up archway/doorway props with no depth, or a multi-panel prop-sheet (c1); round 2 added explicit 'wide receding corridor perspective, deep multi-layered depth, distant vanishing point' positive language plus close-up/isolated-prop negatives -- c4 (isometric floating tile prop) and c6 (torch-lit archway gate, still shallow depth) were rejected as insufficiently deep, and c5 (canyon exterior with visible sky/birds) was rejected as an off-contract landscape scene, leaving c7's genuine tunnel recession as the clear winner.
Provenance.aiDisclosure: AI-generated (SDXL base 1.0) diffuse. Deviation from the standard chain, matching every sibling backdrop (gloomwood/sunkencrypt/mine): cutout.py's BiRefNet salient-object segmentation was NOT run (it discards a full-bleed atmospheric scene as background). Instead the raw 1024x1024 SDXL output was resized (PIL LANCZOS) to 160x160 to match mine-backdrop.png/gloomwood-backdrop.png/sunkencrypt-backdrop.png's identical committed footprint exactly, then format-converted to opaque RGB (no normalmap.py -- AssetSpec.NormalMap=false, flat far plane per EmberfallSpecs.cs). The exact 1024->160 downscale filter used by the original sibling sessions is not recorded in any prior build-half or seeds.generated.md entry; LANCZOS was chosen here as the standard high-quality filter for shrinking painterly/photographic content (as opposed to nearest-neighbour, which this repo reserves for pixel-art upscaling elsewhere).
